title: Daily-vlog per-episode brand kit: neutralize eight differently-lit episode stills to one house white point at the in-frame grey cards, author a warm split-tone look, pop the hero for a thumbnail and vertical cover, vectorize the channel wordmark, and data-merge an eight-page episode style-frame sheet

source.reference: Post-production / colour + supporting graphics for a recurring daily-life vlog channel (per-episode brand kit)

grounding_note: ADAPTED from a real Freelancer.com brief in which a creator films their own day-to-day content and needs recurring per-episode post-production: 'basic colour correction', supporting graphics for lower-thirds and end screens, shot in 4K and delivered as web-ready 1080p, with the supporting custom graphics wanted as deliverables and an ongoing episode-to-episode collaboration. The real creator's handle is laundered to a fully invented channel persona, 'The Halden Diaries' (wordmark 'HALDEN', tagline 'an ordinary week, filmed', run by fictional creator Nate Halden) — no real person, company, channel, product, platform, or trademark is named anywhere; the real source handle is not reproduced. All software is referred to by generic craft terms (a repeatable house grade, page-layout/merge, vector tracing), never by product name; the video-sharing platform and short-form 'story/vertical' surface are described generically as delivery channels. REPOSITIONED for connector reality AND repaired against the audit: the killed original graded only ONE frame-grab plus one still and stamped a canned develop preset (no cross-asset consistency, no authored look, the designed artifact punted), shipped four supplemental video clips that ZERO steps consumed, declared a 1080p clip whose 9:16 reframe would have UPSCALED, and left stale 'generative expand / outpaint' wording. The corrected design keeps the same job the brief rewards — the recurring per-episode STILL brand kit plus the one same-length social reframe the brief names — but routes it to what the connectors genuinely own: the channel keeps a small 18% grey card propped on the desk as a habit, so the week's eight episode key-stills (each shot in whatever light that room and hour happened to have) can be reconciled to ONE house look after the fact; the freelancer neutralizes each still to its own in-frame card, authors a single warm split-tone 'personal, upbeat' look, pops the hero for a thumbnail and vertical cover, vectorizes the wordmark, and DATA-MERGES a genuinely hand-authored single-record page-layout template into a press-ready per-episode style-frame sheet (one episode per page). The unused supplemental clips are removed; the reframe source is declared at true 4K so the vertical is an honest downscale. Nothing is invented beyond the 'colour correction + supporting graphics + social reframe + ongoing per-episode cadence' the client wrote.
one_line_ask: Bring the channel's eight episode key-stills — each shot under different room light with a small 18% grey card on the desk — to ONE consistent house look (each still neutralized to its own in-frame card at a single common white point, then a warm split-tone the freelancer authors), pop the hero episode's creator off its busy background for a channel thumbnail and a vertical story cover, clean the flat wordmark into a razor-sharp scalable mark for lower-thirds and the end screen, reframe one 4K episode take to a same-length vertical, and data-merge the channel's authored single-record layout into an eight-page per-episode style-frame sheet.
full_brief:
I run 'The Halden Diaries', a daily-life vlog. The video edit itself — timeline cutting, jump-cuts, the project file — is handled elsewhere. Your contract is the recurring per-episode STILL BRAND KIT and the one social reframe below, delivered consistently so every week's episodes look like the same channel, week after week.

What you get for this batch:
- Eight episode key-stills, one pulled at the top of each of this week's episodes (episode_still_01 ... episode_still_08). These were shot wherever I happened to be filming — a bright morning window, a warm desk lamp at night, a flat overcast afternoon, late golden light, mixed window-plus-lamp, and so on — so straight out of camera they do NOT match each other; some run cool and dim, some warm and bright. Because I know this happens, I keep a small 18% grey card propped on the desk in shot on every one of them. They are full-resolution camera stills, not tiny web grabs.
- A flat PNG of the channel wordmark lockup ('HALDEN', with the tagline and a small play glyph).
- One ~12s 4K episode take (episode_take_4k.mp4) for the social reframe.
- My channel's episode style-frame sheet layout (halden_episode_sheet.indd) and this week's episode list (episode_kit.csv): eight rows, the episode number, episode title, air date and the segment tag for each, plus the image slots.

What I need back:
- THE EPISODE STYLE-FRAME SHEET (the main deliverable): a press-ready ~300 DPI PDF of my per-episode brand sheet, ONE episode per page, eight pages, that I keep as the channel's reference and hand to my editor so lower-thirds and end screens sit on the same look every week. Each page binds its episode number, title, air date and segment tag from the list, drops that episode's graded hero still into the sheet's hero window, and carries my wordmark crisp in the masthead.
- THE LOOK (this is the whole craft): the eight sheet pages have to read as ONE channel, not eight stills from eight different days. Bring every still to the SAME house look — a warm, personal, upbeat grade that is nonetheless consistent frame to frame. Use the grey card in each still to get them all onto ONE common house white point and one shared exposure feel first: because every still started in different light, how far and which way you move is a per-still decision you judge off that still's own card — a batch that is each 'auto-fixed' to look fine on its own will drift apart at the grey cards and I will send it back. Then put my house character on all eight the same way — the warm, lifted, lively feel the channel is known for. Keep skin natural, not orange; keep it lively, not garish. When you are done, hand me, per still, the white-balance (temperature/tint) and exposure move you dialed and the final pixel size, so I can trust the set was matched to one target rather than eyeballed one at a time.
- THE THUMBNAIL: from the hero episode's graded still, give me a clean channel thumbnail at 1280x720 with me clearly popped off the busy room behind me (the background knocked back so I read first).
- THE VERTICAL COVER: from that same popped hero still, a vertical story/cover at 1080x1920, reframed from the existing pixels only — no re-shoot, no invented canvas.
- THE WORDMARK: my flat wordmark cleaned to a crisp, infinitely-scalable vector so it stays razor-sharp in lower-thirds and on the end screen at any size, and reusable across future episodes.
- THE SOCIAL REFRAME: the ~12s 4K episode take reframed to a same-length 1080x1920 vertical for the story feed — no trimming, no re-cut, just the vertical reframe.

PRINT SIZE: each sheet page drops the hero still into a 190 x 107 mm (16:9) hero window, which at press resolution needs at least ~2244 x 1264 px of real image; the stills are full-resolution camera frames, so a 16:9 crop from the full frame clears that — do not grade on a small proxy or enlarge past what the frame holds. Acceptance: every grey card matched to one common house white point across all eight with the per-still moves reported; the same authored house look on all eight; the thumbnail exactly 1280x720 with the background knocked back; the cover exactly 1080x1920 from existing pixels; the wordmark a crisp vector on every masthead; the reframe exactly 1080x1920 at the take's full runtime; and exactly one sheet page per episode-list row.

inputs.name: episode_still_01.png
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal full-resolution mirrorless camera still, 6000x4000, of a 28-year-old male vlog creator seated at a lived-in home desk, three-quarter framing, candid mid-gesture, real skin pores and stray hair, a busy room behind him (bookshelf, plant, tangled cable, coffee mug). Bright cool morning window light from the left, slightly blue-grey cast, a touch bright and flat. A small neutral 18% grey calibration card is propped upright on the desk near the mug, clearly in shot at the frame edge. Candid documentary vlog realism, not glossy studio, natural shallow depth of field, no on-screen text, no brand names or logos on any object, screen, product or clothing. This is the HERO episode still.
inputs.realism_notes: HERO still (drives the thumbnail + vertical cover). Cast: COOL blue-grey morning window, slightly bright and flat — the agent must WARM it and add contrast to seat its grey card on the common house white point. Same creator identity across all eight. Busy background is deliberate so the subject-pop background knock-down is visibly useful. In-frame 18% grey card is the free checkable WB target; it is RETAINED in the card-bearing master and cropped OUT of the delivered hero/thumbnail/cover. The per-still cast and required direction live here only, never in the brief, the CSV, or the step notes.

inputs.name: episode_still_02.png
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal full-resolution mirrorless camera still, 6000x4000, of the SAME male creator at the same style of home desk at night, lit only by a warm tungsten desk lamp, strong orange cast, dim and low-key, real pores and hair, lived-in room behind. A small neutral 18% grey calibration card propped on the desk, clearly in shot at the frame edge. Candid documentary vlog look, natural depth of field, no on-screen text, no brand names or logos anywhere.
inputs.realism_notes: Cast: strong WARM tungsten, DIM — the agent must COOL the orange cast and LIFT exposure to reach the common house white point; the opposite direction from the cool stills. A single global white-balance or per-still auto-tone cannot converge this with the cool frames at the cards. Grey card retained in the master, cropped from the sheet frame.

inputs.name: episode_still_03.png
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal full-resolution mirrorless camera still, 6000x4000, of the SAME male creator at the desk on a flat overcast afternoon, soft grey north-window light, low contrast, a faint green-grey cast, mildly underexposed, real skin texture, busy room behind. A small neutral 18% grey calibration card propped on the desk, clearly in shot at the frame edge. Candid documentary vlog realism, no on-screen text, no brand names or logos anywhere.
inputs.realism_notes: Cast: FLAT overcast green-grey, low contrast — needs a slight WARM + de-green tint nudge and added contrast to seat its card on the common white point without going muddy. Grey card retained in the master, cropped from the sheet frame.

inputs.name: episode_still_04.png
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal full-resolution mirrorless camera still, 6000x4000, of the SAME male creator at the desk in late golden-hour light, warm and bright, long soft shadows, real pores and hair, lived-in room behind. A small neutral 18% grey calibration card propped on the desk, clearly in shot at the frame edge. Candid documentary vlog look, natural shallow depth of field, no on-screen text, no brand names or logos anywhere.
inputs.realism_notes: Cast: WARM golden, BRIGHT — must be COOLED toward the common white point but only partly, and highlights protected so the bright frame does not clip; a naive 'warm everything' or 'cool everything' batch move breaks against the tungsten and window frames. Grey card retained in the master, cropped from the sheet frame.

inputs.name: episode_still_05.png
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal full-resolution mirrorless camera still, 6000x4000, of the SAME male creator at the desk in mixed light — cool window on one side, warm lamp on the other — a split colour cast across the frame, moderate exposure, real skin texture, busy room behind. A small neutral 18% grey calibration card propped on the desk, clearly in shot at the frame edge. Candid documentary vlog realism, no on-screen text, no brand names or logos anywhere.
inputs.realism_notes: Cast: MIXED / split window-plus-lamp — the hardest WB judgement; the agent must pick the correction that lands THIS still's grey card on the common white point even though the cast is uneven across the frame. Grey card retained in the master, cropped from the sheet frame.

inputs.name: episode_still_06.png
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal full-resolution mirrorless camera still, 6000x4000, of the SAME male creator at the desk under cool overhead fluorescent light, a faint green-cyan cast, even but slightly flat exposure, real pores and hair, lived-in room behind. A small neutral 18% grey calibration card propped on the desk, clearly in shot at the frame edge. Candid documentary vlog look, no on-screen text, no brand names or logos anywhere.
inputs.realism_notes: Cast: COOL fluorescent green-cyan — needs a WARM shift plus a magenta tint nudge to kill the green so its card reads neutral on the common white point. Grey card retained in the master, cropped from the sheet frame.

inputs.name: episode_still_07.png
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal full-resolution mirrorless camera still, 6000x4000, of the SAME male creator at the desk in bright direct noon daylight, near-neutral colour but high-key and slightly overexposed with hot window highlights, real skin texture, busy room behind. A small neutral 18% grey calibration card propped on the desk, clearly in shot at the frame edge. Candid documentary vlog realism, no on-screen text, no brand names or logos anywhere.
inputs.realism_notes: Cast: near-neutral but OVEREXPOSED / high-key — WB barely moves, but exposure/highlights must be PULLED DOWN to match the set's shared exposure feel; over-correcting the colour here pushes it off the group. The real work is tonal, not WB. Grey card retained in the master, cropped from the sheet frame.

inputs.name: episode_still_08.png
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal full-resolution mirrorless camera still, 6000x4000, of the SAME male creator at the desk late in the evening in dim low warm light, underexposed and shadowy, real pores and hair, lived-in room behind. A small neutral 18% grey calibration card propped on the desk, clearly in shot at the frame edge. Candid documentary vlog look, no on-screen text, no brand names or logos anywhere.
inputs.realism_notes: Cast: DIM low-warm evening, UNDEREXPOSED — the biggest EXPOSURE lift in the set plus a modest cool nudge to seat its card on the common white point without lifting shadow noise into mud. Grey card retained in the master, cropped from the sheet frame.

inputs.name: channel_wordmark_flat.png
inputs.gen_prompt: Flat 2D channel logo lockup on a TRANSPARENT background: the wordmark 'HALDEN' in a bold rounded geometric sans, a lowercase tagline 'an ordinary week, filmed' beneath, and a small simple play-triangle glyph to the left, two flat solid brand colours (deep teal and warm coral), crisp clean hard edges, centred with a generous transparent margin all around, no gradients, no photographic texture, no sheen, exported slightly oversized and off-centre, 2400x1200 PNG with alpha.
inputs.realism_notes: Flat, hard-edged, solid-fill text art on transparent alpha so image_vectorize produces clean closed SVG paths after prep-before-trace (crop-to-bounds to strip the generous margin, then a crisp contrast pass so the edges separate hard). Text-bearing wordmark -> gemini-3-pro-image for legible letterforms. A SUPPLIED asset only cropped/crisped/vectorized — no letterform is designed from scratch. Enclosed counters (A, D, O) sit on the light/white ground so they read correctly after tracing; no dark-ground knockout is claimed.

inputs.name: episode_take_4k.mp4
inputs.gen_prompt: A ~12 second handheld 4K horizontal vlog take, 3840x2160 16:9, of the same male creator walking-and-talking to camera through a sunny apartment, casual upbeat energy, slight natural handheld shake, real daylight, candid documentary vlog style, no on-screen text, no brand names or logos on any object, screen, product or clothing.
inputs.realism_notes: Declared at true 4K (3840x2160) so the same-length 9:16 reframe is HONEST: a vertical crop of the 4K frame holds ~1215x2160, so delivering 1080x1920 is a downscale, never an upscale (the killed original declared a 1080p/1920x1088 clip, which would have upscaled to 1080x1920). Horizontal 16:9 so the reframe is meaningful. ~12s real handheld camera take, longer than any target derived from it; video_resize is a same-length reframe, never a trim and never an assembly.

inputs.name: halden_episode_sheet.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED DELIVERABLE (cannot be model-generated): a genuine, hand-built page-layout document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD A4 landscape (297 x 210 mm) per-episode style-frame sheet page with 3 mm bleed — ONE episode per page. It must contain live data-merge placeholder fields <<EpisodeNo>>, <<EpisodeTitle>>, <<AirDate>>, <<Segment>>, and TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a 190 x 107 mm (16:9) hero window bound to @HeroFrame (that episode's graded hero still) and a small masthead lockup frame at the top bound to @Wordmark (the vectorized wordmark). Because free-form image-at-coordinates placement is banned, the wordmark reaches the masthead ONLY as a merge bind through this second image frame — it is not dropped in by hand. The <<EpisodeTitle>> text frame has Auto-Size 'shrink text to fit' enabled so a long title binds without going overset. The sheet furniture (grid rule, caption bar, page ground, brand colour band) is already drawn on every page; the only per-row imagery is the hero window and the masthead wordmark. Built by hand so the merge fields and BOTH image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output and NOT a multi-up contact sheet: the merge emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields; a converted-PDF template or a multi-record-per-page sheet would not bind / cannot be produced.
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real merge fields plus genuine @image-path columns, and it emits ONE FILE PER ROW — so a single-record one-episode-per-page sheet is the correct, connector-doable shape (eight rows => an eight-page sheet), not a multi-up contact sheet. Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd with literal typed text would not bind. TWO image columns (@HeroFrame, @Wordmark) mean the merge resolves two prepped assets per row — the row's graded hero AND the shared vectorized wordmark — so the chain-produced wordmark has a real, connector-doable path onto every masthead without any free-form placement. document_merge_data_vector is text-only and cannot bind an image column, so the layout merge (not the vector merge) is the correct tool. Column names must exactly match the episode-list headers.

inputs.name: episode_kit.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: Generate a CSV with headers exactly: EpisodeNo,EpisodeTitle,AirDate,Segment,@HeroFrame,@Wordmark and 8 rows, one per episode, in episode order. EpisodeNo is 01..08. EpisodeTitle is the human episode title and MUST include at least one deliberately LONG title (e.g. 'The Longest Tuesday of an Ordinary Week', ~40+ chars) alongside short ones (e.g. 'Reset', 'Slow Morning') so the template's shrink-to-fit is exercised. AirDate is a plain date string (e.g. '2026-03-02'). Segment is one of exactly two values: 'Main Episode' or 'Bonus Cut'. @HeroFrame holds the agreed prepped hero-frame filename for that episode (hero_ep01.jpg ... hero_ep08.jpg, in row order) so the merge drops the correct graded still into that page. @Wordmark holds 'channel_mark.svg' on EVERY row (the same vectorized masthead lockup binds onto every page). NO column names any lighting cast, colour temperature, exposure, correction direction, treatment, or output file type — the titles, dates and segment tags are neutral episode metadata only, so the grade direction stays the freelancer's decision from each still's grey card rather than a value read off the CSV. Column names must exactly match the template merge fields <<EpisodeNo>>,<<EpisodeTitle>>,<<AirDate>>,<<Segment>> and the two @image-path columns.
inputs.realism_notes: Eight rows => the merge must produce exactly eight sheet pages (page-count = row-count gate). The @HeroFrame column holds the filenames the agent must produce and upload under those exact names, so naming discipline is a real dependency; @Wordmark repeats the single vectorized SVG so the agent-owned masthead lands on every page. EpisodeTitle/AirDate/Segment are client copy bound verbatim. NOTHING in the CSV encodes the per-still cast, the correction, or the treatment — the @HeroFrame names are neutral (hero_epNN.jpg), so the triage of which still needs which grade is the agent's decision from the cards, never a value handed in the sheet. The long title exercises the auto-fit frame.

outputs.name: HaldenDiaries_EpisodeKit_Sheet_x8.pdf
outputs.spec: THE PRIMARY, AGENT-OWNED DELIVERABLE. A press-ready ~300 DPI A4 landscape (297 x 210 mm) + 3 mm bleed per-episode style-frame sheet PDF, ONE episode per page, EIGHT pages (page-count = episode-list row-count = 8), exported from the one-file-per-row data-merge. Each page binds its EpisodeNo/EpisodeTitle/AirDate/Segment verbatim from the episode list, drops that episode's grey-card-matched, house-graded hero still into the 190 x 107 mm (16:9) hero window (>=2244 x 1264 px so it prints >=300 DPI), and drops the vectorized wordmark into the masthead. The eight pages read as one channel — one common house white point, one shared exposure feel, one authored warm split-tone. The 'hero' is simply page one of the merged sheet (no per-record named export). Its distinctive quality — the matched grade, the authored look, the crisp masthead — is the agent's, not a template default.

outputs.name: episode_still_masters_cardbearing_x8
outputs.spec: Eight grey-card-matched full-resolution masters (native ~6000x4000), one per episode still, each with its in-frame 18% grey card driven onto ONE common house white point and the whole set matched to one shared exposure feel, then carrying the single authored warm split-tone look. The grey card is RETAINED in frame in these masters — this is the grade-audit artifact the grader checks white-point agreement on (the card is cropped OUT of the delivered hero frames, so consistency is graded here, on the retained card-bearing masters, not on the delivered sheet). Accompanied by a report of the final white-balance (temperature/tint) and exposure move AND the final pixel dimensions of each still.

outputs.name: episode_hero_frames_x8
outputs.spec: Eight 16:9 hero crops (hero_ep01.jpg ... hero_ep08.jpg), each cropped from the FULL-resolution card-bearing master to the 190 x 107 mm (16:9) hero-window ratio with the grey card cropped OUT, held at >=2244 x 1264 px so each prints >=300 DPI in the window. These are the @HeroFrame assets the merge resolves per row; card-exclusion is checked here, separately from the white-point check on the masters.

outputs.name: thumbnail_1280x720.png
outputs.spec: Channel thumbnail, 1280x720 16:9, from the hero episode's graded still with the creator subject popped against a saturation-knocked-back busy background (subject masked, background desaturated through the inverted mask, then cropped/downscaled from the full-resolution popped still).

outputs.name: story_cover_1080x1920.png
outputs.spec: Vertical story/cover still, 1080x1920, a subject-aware reframe/crop of the full-resolution subject-popped hero still to the 9:16 crop using existing pixels only (no re-shoot, no invented canvas, no upscale).

outputs.name: channel_mark.svg
outputs.spec: The flat channel wordmark cleaned and vectorized to a crisp, infinitely-scalable SVG (prep-before-trace: crop-to-bounds then a crisp contrast pass then trace), razor-sharp for lower-thirds and the end screen at any size, bound into every sheet masthead via the @Wordmark column and reusable on future episodes.

outputs.name: episode_clip_vertical_9x16.mp4
outputs.spec: The ~12s 4K episode take reframed to 1080x1920, SAME length as the source (subject-aware reframe only, no trim, no re-cut, no format-conversion claim). The 4K height carries a 9:16 crop of ~1215x2160, so 1080x1920 is an honest downscale, never an upscale. Frame-accurate cuts and motion graphics are the elsewhere-handled edit, not claimed here. [async]

connector_workflow.inputs_from: episode_still_01.png, episode_still_02.png, episode_still_03.png, episode_still_04.png, episode_still_05.png, episode_still_06.png, episode_still_07.png, episode_still_08.png
connector_workflow.note: Initialize a block upload of the eight client episode key-stills into the channel's Creative Cloud project folder. Plumbing only — not the difficulty.
Finalize the upload; yields stable asset URIs for the eight episode stills that the grade sub-chains reference.

Neutralize episode_still_01's in-frame 18% grey card onto the ONE common house white point and bring its exposure onto the set's shared feel. How far and which way (temperature/tint/exposure) is judged BY EYE from THIS still's card until the card looks neutral at the group point — the agent never reads a pixel value. Establish this as the house target the other seven must hit. Card RETAINED in frame -> card-bearing master. Primitive-built adjustments, not a preset and not auto_tone. Report the applied move and final px.

Author the channel house look on the neutralized master: a warm, personal, upbeat split-tone the freelancer decides and then applies IDENTICALLY across all eight — a moderate, bounded lift/warm-shift of the orange/red skin band and a gentle desaturation-and-cool of the blue/aqua shadow band (well under a 90-degree hue rotation; no complementary swing). This is the agent-authored look built from primitives, not a canned develop preset. Card still retained.

Crop the grey card OUT and reframe on the creator to the 190 x 107 mm (16:9) hero window, taken from the FULL 6000x4000 master so it holds >=2244 x 1264 px (clears 300 DPI in the window). onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never canvas-extend, never upscale. Report final px. Uploaded later as hero_ep01.jpg.

Neutralize episode_still_02's in-frame grey card onto the SAME common house white point and match its exposure to the set — the required direction depends on this still's own cast, judged by eye from its card, and is NOT the same move as still 01. A single global white-balance or per-still auto-tone would leave this still disagreeing with 01 at the cards. Card retained. Report the applied move and final px.
Apply the SAME authored house split-tone (identical bounded skin-warm / shadow-cool move) as still 01 so the set shares one character. Card retained.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 16:9 hero window from the full master at >=2244 x 1264 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. hero_ep02.jpg.
Neutralize episode_still_03's grey card onto the common house white point and match exposure, direction judged by eye from this still's own card. Card retained. Report the applied move and final px.
Apply the SAME authored house split-tone. Card retained.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 16:9 hero window from the full master at >=2244 x 1264 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. hero_ep03.jpg.

Neutralize episode_still_04's grey card onto the common house white point and match exposure, protecting the bright highlights so the frame does not clip; direction judged by eye from this still's own card. Card retained. Report the applied move and final px.
Apply the SAME authored house split-tone. Card retained.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 16:9 hero window from the full master at >=2244 x 1264 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. hero_ep04.jpg.

Neutralize episode_still_05's grey card onto the common house white point and match exposure — the hardest judgement of the set because the cast is uneven across the frame; drive the card itself neutral at the group point by eye. Card retained. Report the applied move and final px.
Apply the SAME authored house split-tone. Card retained.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 16:9 hero window from the full master at >=2244 x 1264 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. hero_ep05.jpg.
Neutralize episode_still_06's grey card onto the common house white point and match exposure, judged by eye from this still's own card. Card retained. Report the applied move and final px.
Apply the SAME authored house split-tone. Card retained.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 16:9 hero window from the full master at >=2244 x 1264 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. hero_ep06.jpg.

Neutralize episode_still_07 onto the set: here the white-balance barely moves but exposure/highlights must come DOWN to match the group's shared feel; judged by eye from this still's own card and the clipped highlights. Over-moving the colour pushes it off the group. Card retained. Report the applied move and final px.
Apply the SAME authored house split-tone. Card retained.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 16:9 hero window from the full master at >=2244 x 1264 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. hero_ep07.jpg.

Neutralize episode_still_08 onto the set: the largest exposure LIFT of the group plus a WB nudge so its grey card lands on the common house white point without lifting shadow noise into mud; judged by eye from this still's own card. With this still done, all eight share one white point, each neutralized to its own retained card by its own decision. Card retained. Report the applied move and final px.
Apply the SAME authored house split-tone so all eight share one character. Card retained.
Crop the card out, reframe to the 16:9 hero window from the full master at >=2244 x 1264 px. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only. Report final px. hero_ep08.jpg.
Semantically mask the creator on the graded HERO master (ep01_looked) for the subject-pop thumbnail. A semantic subject selection, not a hue/region/coordinate selection.
Invert the subject mask so the correction targets the busy room behind the creator, not the creator.

Knock the background saturation (and a touch of clarity/exposure) DOWN through the inverted mask so the creator reads first — a masked selective edit, not a whole-image overlay. This is the popped hero the thumbnail and vertical cover both derive from.

Crop the card OUT and reframe the popped hero to a clean 1280x720 16:9 channel thumbnail from the full-resolution popped still. onSubjectClipping='extract', downscale-only, never upscale. -> deliverable.

Subject-aware reframe/crop the full-resolution popped hero to a 1080x1920 9:16 vertical story/cover using existing pixels only (focus: subject, reframe within existing pixels, card cropped out, no invented canvas). A 9:16 crop of the 6000x4000 master is ~2250x4000, so 1080x1920 is an honest downscale. -> deliverable.
Initialize a block upload of the flat wordmark (transparent alpha) so it can be prepped and vectorized for the sheet masthead. Plumbing.
Finalize the wordmark upload into a real CC image asset URL to drive the prep-before-trace chain.

Prep-before-trace step 1: crop the oversized/off-centre wordmark to the tight bounds of the glyphs (strips the generous transparent margin) so the trace sees only the lettering, tagline and play glyph, not empty canvas.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast and set the black/white points so the two solid brand-colour fills separate hard-edged from the transparent ground — a soft raster traces into ragged, doubled edges.

Trace the prepared flat wordmark into clean closed SVG paths (channel_mark.svg) for a razor-sharp masthead on every sheet page and reuse in lower-thirds/end screens. Vectorize of a SUPPLIED, prepared flat mark on a light ground (enclosed counters read correctly) — no letterform designed. FINAL vector deliverable and the @Wordmark asset the merge binds.
Initialize a block upload of the ~12s 4K episode take (media_type video/mp4) for the same-length vertical reframe. Plumbing.
Finalize the take upload into a real CC video assetId with a fetchable URL for the reframe.

Reframe the ~12s 4K take to a clean full-length 9:16 1080x1920 vertical for the story feed, SAME runtime as the source (subject-aware reframe, no trim, no re-cut). The 4K height carries the 9:16 crop (~1215x2160) so 1080x1920 is an honest downscale, never an upscale. [A] async-widget; the product polls + notifies. FINAL video deliverable.

chaining_note: Strict output-to-input chaining. Steps 1-2 load the eight episode stills (stills_assets). GRADE SPINE (the core): each of the eight stills drives its own three-step sub-chain — an image_apply_adjustments neutralization to ITS OWN in-frame 18% grey card at the ONE common house white point (adaptive and non-identical per still: warm the cool window/fluorescent/evening frames, cool the tungsten/golden frames, pull exposure on the overexposed noon frame, lift the dim evening frame hardest, resolve the mixed-cast frame by eye), whose output is the RETAINED card-bearing master (ep01_master..ep08_master); then an image_adjust_hsl applying the SAME authored warm split-tone look across all eight (identical bounded skin-warm / shadow-cool move) -> epNN_looked; then an image_crop_and_resize that crops the grey card OUT and reframes to the 16:9 hero window from the FULL 6000x4000 master at >=2244x1264 px -> hero_epNN. Steps 3-26 are these eight sub-chains. THUMBNAIL/COVER BRANCH off the hero (ep01_looked): image_select_subject (27) -> image_invert_selection (28) -> masked image_apply_adjustments desaturating the background (29 -> hero_popped) -> image_crop_and_resize to 1280x720 (30 = thumbnail) and image_crop_and_resize to 1080x1920 (31 = story cover), both downscales of the full-res popped still. WORDMARK BRANCH: upload-init (32) -> finalize (33 -> wordmark_asset) -> image_crop_to_bounds (34) -> crisp image_apply_adjustments (35) -> image_vectorize (36 -> channel_mark.svg). VIDEO BRANCH: upload-init (37) -> finalize (38 -> take_asset) -> video_resize (39 -> episode_clip_vertical_9x16 [A]). CONVERGENCE: the eight hero frames and the vectorized wordmark fan into the merge upload session (40) -> finalize (41 -> merge_asset_urns) -> document_merge_data_layout (42), which also consumes the authored single-record .indd and the episode-list CSV and emits one page per row resolving BOTH @HeroFrame and @Wordmark; the merged set exports to the per-episode press PDF (43). The only non-chained calls are the four standard upload-init idioms (1,32,37,40), each immediately consumed by its finalize; everything else sets inputs_from to a producing step's output. No banned capability: zero generative calls (no text-to-image, no generative fill/expand, no compositing, no upscaling, no from-scratch art/logo, no object removal, no bg-replace-by-prompt), video_resize is a same-length reframe (no trim/convert), the merge places one record per page (no N-up), no convert_pdf_to_indd, no image_fill_area, no image_apply_color_overlay, and the hsl look stays well under a 90-degree rotation.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship: 43 connector calls, 12 distinct Adobe tools across three groups (asset I/O, the photo/raster image_* family, the async video reframe, and the [T]/[C] page-layout merge) — well past the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the four upload idioms (8 plumbing calls), leaving 35 difficulty-bearing steps. Difficulty is DEPTH, not breadth or plumbing: the core is eight DIFFERENT reasoned grade decisions, in different and sometimes opposite directions, all forced to converge on one measurable target (each still's own static in-frame 18% grey card at one common house white point) even though the eight stills were shot in eight different lights — warm the cool window/fluorescent/evening frames, cool the tungsten/golden frames, pull exposure on the blown noon frame, lift the dim evening frame hardest, resolve the mixed-cast frame by eye — so a blanket batch correction or per-still auto-tone visibly fails to match at the cards. On top of the technical match sits an agent-AUTHORED look built from primitives — a warm split-tone the freelancer reasons to and applies identically (a bounded image_adjust_hsl skin-warm / shadow-cool move under 90 degrees), not a canned develop preset (which the killed original leaned on). Layered further: a masked subject-pop (select_subject -> invert -> masked desaturate) that must knock the busy background without touching the creator; prep-before-trace wordmark discipline (crop-to-bounds -> crisp -> vectorize) on a light-ground mark whose enclosed counters read correctly; camera-scale reasoning (a 16:9 hero window at 300 DPI can only be met by cropping from the full 6000x4000 frame, and the 1080x1920 reframe is honest only because the take is true 4K, never an upscale); and a two-image-column, one-file-per-row merge into a hand-authored single-record template ending in an agent-OWNED press-ready eight-page sheet. Respects every hard limit: image_crop_and_resize downscale-only with onSubjectClipping='extract', video_resize same-runtime reframe (no trim, no upscale), no generative fill/expand/text-to-image/object-removal/from-scratch art, no image_fill_area, no image_apply_color_overlay, no auto_tone in the correct path (auto_tone is the named trap), no >90-degree hsl rotation, convert_pdf_to_indd NOT used, the merge places one record per page (no N-up), and document_merge_data_vector (text-only) is correctly avoided in favour of the layout merge for the image columns. Deprecated tools (image_adjust_color_temperature/_highlights/_vibrance_and_saturation/_brightness_and_contrast) are replaced by image_apply_adjustments.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): the eight sheet pages must read as ONE channel — every still's in-frame 18% grey card driven to one common house white point with the set on one shared exposure feel, then the one authored warm split-tone on all eight — and because the stills were shot in eight different lights, each needs its OWN, sometimes opposite, correction judged from its own card; running one global white-balance or per-still auto_tone (which keys off each frame's own histogram) leaves the cool window/fluorescent/evening frames disagreeing with the warm tungsten/golden frames at the grey cards and the sheet is rejected, and the agent must REPORT the per-still temperature/tint/exposure move and final pixel size so 'matched' is auditable rather than asserted. Two further checkable gates back it: every hero frame must clear >=2244 x 1264 px (so it prints >=300 DPI in the 190 x 107 mm 16:9 window) and the merged PDF page-count must equal the episode-list row-count (8), since the layout merge is one-file-per-row. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS (>=2): (1) cross-asset consistency to a measurable common white point across eight differently-lit stills, each requiring a different, sometimes opposite correction reasoned to its own retained grey card — not one set of sliders — plus an authored look applied uniformly on top; (2) constraint-reasoning around tool limitations — a 16:9 print hero can only be derived from the full-resolution frame so it just clears the 300 DPI floor with no upscaling permitted anywhere (the same reasoning that makes the 1080x1920 reframe honest only because the source is true 4K), plus prep-before-trace wordmark discipline and the two-image-column one-record-per-page merge. TRAP (the brief states only the goal 'the pages have to read as one channel' and leaves the method to the agent; the per-still casts live only in inputs[].realism_notes): the naive path auto-tones or globally corrects each still so each looks fine alone, which passes a thumbnail but drifts apart at the grey cards and fails the one-white-point gate; a second pitfall is cropping the grey card out BEFORE neutralizing (destroying the reference) — which is why white-point agreement is graded on the RETAINED card-bearing masters and card-exclusion is checked separately on the hero frames; a third is stamping a canned develop preset for the 'house look' instead of authoring the split-tone; a fourth is grading on a downscaled proxy or declaring a 1080p reframe source, dropping under the print/vertical floor. MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (grader-side, the agent never measures): all eight grey cards agree at the one common house white point on the retained masters with per-still WB/exposure reported and non-identical across the warm vs cool stills; the same authored split-tone on all eight; every hero frame >=2244 x 1264 px with final px reported; the thumbnail exactly 1280x720 with the background knocked back; the cover exactly 1080x1920 from existing pixels; the reframe exactly 1080x1920 at the take's full runtime; the wordmark a crisp vector on every masthead; and exactly one press-ready ~300 DPI A4 sheet page per episode-list row.
